entries.subject: DAMIT 304: selected shape and spin
entries.finding: The official DAMIT metadata export was joined by model and asteroid identity and compared with the selected local recipe shape/model-304.txt. Model 304, version 2011-02-18, pole (266°, 5°), period 5.750249 h match the retained metadata. The archive supplies no diameter for this model; a separate scale constraint is required. This comparison checks source identity and metadata, not fresh mesh bytes, registration or the completeness of other archives.

entries.subject: Marciniak (2011), Photometry and models of selected main belt asteroids. VIII. Low-pole asteroids
entries.finding: [Marciniak (2011), Photometry and models of selected main belt asteroids. VIII. Low-pole asteroids](https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011A%26A...529A.107M) — original model publication record.

entries.subject: AKARI AcuA
entries.finding: [AKARI AcuA](https://data.darts.isas.jaxa.jp/pub/akari/AKARI-IRC_Catalogue_AllSky_AcuA_1.0/) — included as an explicitly approximate thermal size transfer. Its fitted nonrotating-sphere diameter is 64.08 ± 0.77 km. Formal catalog error omits additional shape, spin and thermal-model effects; no total confidence interval is invented. The original catalogue row for asteroid 174 was retrieved again and matched field-for-field with the retained row, including diameter, reported error and detection count.

entries.subject: PDS SBN catalogue values that disagree with the factsheet or are not shown
entries.finding: The display scale "32.04 km (approximate thermal scale)" (akari-acua-v1) implies a diameter of 64.08 km, outside the added NEOWISE V2.0 neowise_mainbelt.csv record 130 (Masiero et al. 2014) diameter 64.849 ± 0.392 km (NEOWISE, NEATM). Both are shown; the display scale is not changed.
entries.revisitWhen: A newer release of the named catalogue, or a review that replaces the shown value.
